title: The Source of Data Value: Consumer Disclosure, Access Design, and Platform Monetization
abstract: arXiv:2610.22864v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Digital marketplaces increasingly earn revenue from transaction commissions and seller-facing data services. Sellers may purchase data to increase revenue or avoid competing with an informed rival. We examine how consumer disclosure rights shape these motives and the platform's incentive to provide data. We develop a game-theoretic model of a commissioned platform, two differentiated sellers, and privacy-sensitive consumers. Data generates value through bilateral sales-revenue gains and competition threats arising from asymmetric access. Under mandatory collection, the platform can monetize defensive adoption, even when bilateral personalization reduces seller revenue. Under voluntary disclosure, anonymous purchasing and strictly positive privacy costs make unilateral disclosure unattractive in the baseline. Exclusive access thus yields no usable information, restores sellers' no-data rejection payoffs, and eliminates defensive fees. P

translated_title: 数据价值的来源：消费者披露、访问设计与平台变现
translated_abstract: 数字市场日益从交易佣金和面向卖家的数据服务中获取收入。卖家可能购买数据以增加收入，或避免与掌握信息的竞争对手展开竞争。我们研究了消费者披露权利如何塑造这些动机以及平台提供数据的激励。我们建立了一个由佣金制平台、两个差异化卖家和隐私敏感消费者构成的博弈论模型。数据通过双边销售收入增益以及由非对称访问引发的竞争威胁产生价值。在强制收集制度下，即使双边个性化会降低卖家收入，平台仍可通过卖家的防御性数据购买实现变现。在自愿披露制度下，匿名购买和严格为正的隐私成本使得单方面披露在基准情形下不具吸引力。因此，独占访问不会产生任何可用信息，恢复了卖家在无数据情形下的拒绝收益，并消除了防御性费用。
tldr: 本文通过博弈论模型揭示了消费者披露权利如何影响平台数据变现机制：在强制收集制度下平台可通过卖家的防御性数据购买获利，而在自愿披露制度下匿名购买与隐私成本使披露不具吸引力，从而消除防御性费用。
en_tdlr: Using a game-theoretic model, this paper shows how consumer disclosure rights shape platform data monetization: under mandatory collection, platforms can profit from sellers' defensive data purchases, while under voluntary disclosure, anonymous purchasing and positive privacy costs make disclosure unattractive, eliminating defensive fees.
